name: Ibrāhīm
meaning: Abraham (Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him)
revelation_details: Makkan (52 verses, revealed in Makkah during a time of heavy persecution and rejection against Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the early Muslims).
core_theme: This Surah is a powerful message of light, gratitude, and unshakable faith. Revealed when the Muslims were weak and mocked, it reminds believers that Allah's message brings people out of darkness into light. Through the stories of past prophets, a chilling speech from Shaytan on Judgment Day, and the heartfelt prayers of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), it teaches that gratitude brings endless blessings, while arrogance and ingratitude lead to total ruin.
name_origin:
The Surah gets its name from Prophet Ibrahim (AS), whose deeply moving prayers and story in the barren valley of Makkah appear in verses 35-41. Naming this Makkan chapter after Ibrahim (AS) carries a sharp, direct message for the people of Makkah.

The Historical Context (A Message to the Quraysh): The pagan leaders of Makkah took immense pride in being the descendants of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the caretakers of the Kaaba. Yet, at the exact same time, they filled the Kaaba with idols and tortured Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) for calling them to worship Allah alone.

By naming this Surah after Ibrahim (AS) and recording his exact prayers, Allah exposed their hypocrisy. Ibrahim (AS) had specifically prayed for Makkah to be a city of peace and begged Allah to keep him and his children far away from worshipping idols. Through this Surah, Allah reminds the Quraysh - and every believer - that true connection to Ibrahim (AS) is not about bloodline or pride; it is about pure monotheism, gratitude, and trusting Allah completely.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: From Darkness to Light and the Language of Messengers

points.label: The Book of Light
points.detail: The chapter opens with the distinct letters (Alif-Lam-Ra) and declares that Allah revealed the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to bring humanity out of the depths of darkness into light, by their Lord's permission, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

points.label: The Owner of Everything
points.detail: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone. Severe punishment awaits the disbelievers who prefer this temporary worldly life over the Hereafter, block others from Allah's path, and try to make it look crooked - they are far astray.

points.label: Clear Communication
points.detail: Allah never sent a messenger except speaking the language of his own people so he could explain the message clearly. After the truth is made plain, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Book of Light: The chapter opens with the distinct letters (Alif-Lam-Ra) and declares that Allah revealed the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to bring humanity out of the depths of darkness into light, by their Lord's permission, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
• The Owner of Everything: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone. Severe punishment awaits the disbelievers who prefer this temporary worldly life over the Hereafter, block others from Allah's path, and try to make it look crooked - they are far astray.
• Clear Communication: Allah never sent a messenger except speaking the language of his own people so he could explain the message clearly. After the truth is made plain, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir point out that the Quran uses the plural for darkness (zulumat - ignorance, disbelief, and sin) and the singular for light (nur - the one straight path of guidance). Sending every prophet in his people's own native tongue shows Allah's fairness: no community can ever claim they failed to understand the message.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Prophet Musa (AS), the "Days of Allah," and the Law of Gratitude

points.label: Reminding People of the "Days of Allah
points.detail: Allah sent Prophet Musa (AS) with clear signs to bring his people out of darkness into light and remind them of the "Days of Allah" (Ayyamillah) - filled with lessons for every deeply patient and grateful person (sabbar shakur).

points.label: Rescue From Pharaoh
points.detail: Musa (AS) reminded the Children of Israel of Allah's immense favor when He saved them from Pharaoh's people, who tortured them cruelly, slaughtered their baby boys, and spared their women - a tremendous trial from their Lord.

points.label: The Universal Promise of Gratitude
points.detail: Musa (AS) conveyed Allah's famous declaration: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you are ungrateful, indeed, My punishment is severe.

points.label: Allah Needs No One
points.detail: Musa (AS) added a humbling truth: even if you and everyone on earth together disbelieve, Allah is completely Free of Need (Ghani) and Worthy of all praise (Hamid).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Reminding People of the "Days of Allah": Allah sent Prophet Musa (AS) with clear signs to bring his people out of darkness into light and remind them of the "Days of Allah" (Ayyamillah) - filled with lessons for every deeply patient and grateful person (sabbar shakur).
• Rescue From Pharaoh: Musa (AS) reminded the Children of Israel of Allah's immense favor when He saved them from Pharaoh's people, who tortured them cruelly, slaughtered their baby boys, and spared their women - a tremendous trial from their Lord.
• The Universal Promise of Gratitude: Musa (AS) conveyed Allah's famous declaration: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you are ungrateful, indeed, My punishment is severe."
• Allah Needs No One: Musa (AS) added a humbling truth: even if you and everyone on earth together disbelieve, Allah is completely Free of Need (Ghani) and Worthy of all praise (Hamid).
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir explains that the "Days of Allah" refer to both Allah's great blessings upon His servants and His punishments upon past oppressors. Pairing patience (sabr) and gratitude (shukr) in verse 5 reflects the authentic Hadith in Sahih Muslim (2999), where the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) taught that a believer's affair is always good: when ease comes they are grateful, and when hardship strikes they are patient.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Past Nations and the Calm Logic of the Messengers

points.label: Stubbornness of Past Nations
points.detail: Allah recalls the stories of earlier peoples - the nations of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, and others known only to Allah. When their messengers brought clear proofs, they pushed their hands into their mouths out of anger and mockery, claiming to be in grave doubt about the message.

points.label: Simple, Undeniable Logic
points.detail: The messengers replied: "Can there be any doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth?" He calls you to forgive your sins. The arrogant leaders objected: "You are only human beings like us! You want to turn us away from what our fathers worshipped - bring us clear proof!

points.label: Humility and Complete Trust
points.detail: The messengers humbly agreed they were only humans, but Allah bestows His favor (prophethood) upon whomever He wills, and no miracle happens except by Allah's permission. They vowed to put their complete trust (tawakkul) in Allah and bear all persecution with patience.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Stubbornness of Past Nations: Allah recalls the stories of earlier peoples - the nations of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, and others known only to Allah. When their messengers brought clear proofs, they pushed their hands into their mouths out of anger and mockery, claiming to be in grave doubt about the message.
• Simple, Undeniable Logic: The messengers replied: "Can there be any doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth?" He calls you to forgive your sins. The arrogant leaders objected: "You are only human beings like us! You want to turn us away from what our fathers worshipped - bring us clear proof!"
• Humility and Complete Trust: The messengers humbly agreed they were only humans, but Allah bestows His favor (prophethood) upon whomever He wills, and no miracle happens except by Allah's permission. They vowed to put their complete trust (tawakkul) in Allah and bear all persecution with patience.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars highlight how the prophets responded to insult and mockery not with anger, but with clarity and tawakkul (reliance on Allah). Asking "Can there be doubt about Allah?" shows that recognizing the Creator is built into sound human reason - the real barrier for past nations was blind loyalty to their forefathers' habits.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Threats of Expulsion, Allah's Promise, and the Fate of Tyrants

points.label: Threats Against the Prophets
points.detail: The disbelievers threatened their messengers: "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion.

points.label: Allah's Promise of Victory
points.detail: At that moment of extreme threat, Allah revealed to the messengers: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers and settle you in the land after them." This promise belongs to those who fear standing before Allah and fear His warning.

points.label: The Ruin of Arrogant Tyrants
points.detail: The messengers sought Allah's help, and every stubborn, arrogant tyrant (jabbar 'anid) ended in complete loss. Ahead of him is Hell, where he will be forced to sip boiling, foul water that he can barely swallow; death surrounds him from every side, yet he cannot die, and harsh torment awaits him.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Threats Against the Prophets: The disbelievers threatened their messengers: "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion."
• Allah's Promise of Victory: At that moment of extreme threat, Allah revealed to the messengers: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers and settle you in the land after them." This promise belongs to those who fear standing before Allah and fear His warning.
• The Ruin of Arrogant Tyrants: The messengers sought Allah's help, and every stubborn, arrogant tyrant (jabbar 'anid) ended in complete loss. Ahead of him is Hell, where he will be forced to sip boiling, foul water that he can barely swallow; death surrounds him from every side, yet he cannot die, and harsh torment awaits him.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators note that these verses were revealed during a peak period of persecution in Makkah when the Quraysh were plotting to drive Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and the believers out. Allah reassured them that throughout history, arrogant tyrants who try to silence the truth are always the ones who end in ruin, while the patient believers inherit the earth.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Worthless Deeds of Disbelief and Allah's Absolute Power

points.label: Ashes in a Storm
points.detail: Allah gives a vivid parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord: all their worldly deeds are like ashes blown away furiously by a fierce wind on a stormy day - they will have zero control over anything they earned, for they strayed far from the truth.

points.label: Creation in Truth
points.detail: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth and with purpose?

points.label: Replacing Humanity Is Easy for Allah
points.detail: If Allah wills, He can remove humanity entirely and bring a completely new creation in its place - and that is not difficult for Allah at all.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Ashes in a Storm: Allah gives a vivid parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord: all their worldly deeds are like ashes blown away furiously by a fierce wind on a stormy day - they will have zero control over anything they earned, for they strayed far from the truth.
• Creation in Truth: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth and with purpose?
• Replacing Humanity Is Easy for Allah: If Allah wills, He can remove humanity entirely and bring a completely new creation in its place - and that is not difficult for Allah at all.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir and As-Sa'di explain that the image of ashes scattered by a stormy wind teaches a crucial lesson: sincere faith (iman) is the foundation that holds good deeds together. Without belief in Allah, even outwardly charitable actions lose their spiritual weight on the Day of Judgment.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Blaming Leaders and the Chilling Sermon of Shaytan

points.label: Followers Confronting Their Leaders
points.detail: On the Day of Judgment, everyone will stand exposed before Allah. The weak followers will beg their arrogant leaders: "We used to follow you - can you protect us from even a small part of Allah's punishment?" The leaders will helplessly reply: "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It makes no difference now whether we panic or stay patient - there is no escape for us.

points.label: Shaytan's Speech in Hell
points.detail: Once judgment is settled, Shaytan will stand up and address his followers: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me - blame yourselves! I cannot help you, and you cannot help me. Indeed, I reject your associating me with Allah before.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Followers Confronting Their Leaders: On the Day of Judgment, everyone will stand exposed before Allah. The weak followers will beg their arrogant leaders: "We used to follow you - can you protect us from even a small part of Allah's punishment?" The leaders will helplessly reply: "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It makes no difference now whether we panic or stay patient - there is no escape for us."
• Shaytan's Speech in Hell: Once judgment is settled, Shaytan will stand up and address his followers: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me - blame yourselves! I cannot help you, and you cannot help me. Indeed, I reject your associating me with Allah before.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars describe verse 22 as one of the most chilling scenes in the entire Quran. For the first time in history, the master of lies speaks the complete, brutal truth - only after it is far too late to repent. It removes every excuse for sin: Shaytan can only whisper and invite, never force anyone against their will.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Eternal Peace of the Righteous

points.label: Gardens of Paradise
points.detail: In direct contrast to the chaos of Hell, those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, living there forever by their Lord's permission.

points.label: The Greeting of Peace
points.detail: Their greeting within Paradise will be "Salam" (Peace).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Gardens of Paradise: In direct contrast to the chaos of Hell, those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, living there forever by their Lord's permission.
• The Greeting of Peace: Their greeting within Paradise will be "Salam" (Peace).
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars admire the placement of this single verse immediately after Shaytan's bitter speech. After hearing the mutual blame and despair of the people of Hell, the believer's heart is immediately comforted by the calm, eternal peace (Salam) awaiting those who stayed faithful.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Parable of the Two Trees and the Firm Word

points.label: The Good Word (The Date Palm)
points.detail: Allah compares a "good word" (La ilaha illallah) to a good tree: its roots are deeply planted in the earth, its branches reach high into the sky, and it yields its fruit in every season by its Lord's permission.

points.label: The Evil Word (The Uprooted Vine)
points.detail: In contrast, an "evil word" (disbelief and falsehood) is like an evil, bitter tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no deep roots and no stability at all.

points.label: Kept Firm in Both Worlds
points.detail: Allah keeps firm those who believe with the "firm word" (al-qawl ath-thabit) in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, while leaving the wrongdoers astray - for Allah does whatever He wills.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Good Word (The Date Palm): Allah compares a "good word" (La ilaha illallah) to a good tree: its roots are deeply planted in the earth, its branches reach high into the sky, and it yields its fruit in every season by its Lord's permission.
• The Evil Word (The Uprooted Vine): In contrast, an "evil word" (disbelief and falsehood) is like an evil, bitter tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no deep roots and no stability at all.
• Kept Firm in Both Worlds: Allah keeps firm those who believe with the "firm word" (al-qawl ath-thabit) in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, while leaving the wrongdoers astray - for Allah does whatever He wills.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Two famous authentic Hadiths illuminate these verses. First, in Sahih al-Bukhari (61, 4698) and Sahih Muslim (2811e), the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) identified the "good tree" as the date palm - steady, deeply rooted, and beneficial in every way, just like a true believer. Second, in Sahih al-Bukhari (4699) and Sahih Muslim (2871a), the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) explained that "the firm word" in verse 27 refers to the questioning in the grave, when Allah keeps the believer's heart and tongue steady so they clearly testify to their Lord, their religion, and their Prophet.

points.label: Exchanging Favor for Ingratitude
points.detail: Allah draws attention to those leaders who exchanged Allah's greatest favor for disbelief and led their own people down into the home of ruin - Hellfire, a wretched resting place.

points.label: Setting Up Rivals
points.detail: They set up false partners alongside Allah to mislead people from His straight path.

points.label: Brief Enjoyment
points.detail: Allah commands the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to tell them: "Enjoy yourselves for a little while, for your final destination is the Fire.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Exchanging Favor for Ingratitude: Allah draws attention to those leaders who exchanged Allah's greatest favor for disbelief and led their own people down into the home of ruin - Hellfire, a wretched resting place.
• Setting Up Rivals: They set up false partners alongside Allah to mislead people from His straight path.
• Brief Enjoyment: Allah commands the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to tell them: "Enjoy yourselves for a little while, for your final destination is the Fire.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: In an authentic narration in Sahih al-Bukhari (4700), Ibn Abbas (RA) explained that these verses referred directly to the arrogant polytheist leaders of Makkah who rejected Allah's greatest blessing - sending Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) among them - and dragged their followers to destruction. It warns that toxic leadership can ruin an entire community.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Commands to Believers and Allah's Uncountable Blessings

points.label: Prayer and Charity Before It Is Too Late
points.detail: Allah tells the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to instruct His believing servants to establish regular prayer and spend in charity - both secretly and openly - from what He provided them, before a Day arrives when there will be no buying, selling, or saving friendships.

points.label: Signs of Provision in Nature
points.detail: Allah created the heavens and the earth, sent down rain from the sky to grow fruits as sustenance, and subjected ships to sail the seas by His command along with flowing rivers for humanity's use.

points.label: The Sun, Moon, Night, and Day
points.detail: Allah subjected the sun and moon moving constantly in their orbits, and subjected the night and the day for human benefit.

points.label: Countless Favors
points.detail: Allah has given humanity from everything they asked of Him: "And if you should try to count the favors of Allah, you could never enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Prayer and Charity Before It Is Too Late: Allah tells the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to instruct His believing servants to establish regular prayer and spend in charity - both secretly and openly - from what He provided them, before a Day arrives when there will be no buying, selling, or saving friendships.
• Signs of Provision in Nature: Allah created the heavens and the earth, sent down rain from the sky to grow fruits as sustenance, and subjected ships to sail the seas by His command along with flowing rivers for humanity's use.
• The Sun, Moon, Night, and Day: Allah subjected the sun and moon moving constantly in their orbits, and subjected the night and the day for human benefit.
• Countless Favors: Allah has given humanity from everything they asked of Him: "And if you should try to count the favors of Allah, you could never enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators highlight how these verses link gratitude to action. Recognizing that Allah has placed the entire universe - rain, rivers, oceans, sunlight, and rest - at our service should naturally move a believer to worship Him in prayer and share His blessings generously with others before Judgment Day arrives.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Heartfelt Prayers of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in Makkah

points.label: Peace for Makkah and Protection From Idols
points.detail: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) prayed: "My Lord, make this city (Makkah) peaceful and secure, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols." Recognizing that idols had misled many people, he affirmed that whoever follows his pure faith belongs to him, while leaving those who disobey to Allah's forgiveness and mercy.

points.label: Settling His Family in a Barren Valley
points.detail: Having left his wife Hajar and baby son Ismail in the empty desert of Makkah by Allah's command, Ibrahim (AS) prayed: "Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House so that they may establish prayer. So make people's hearts incline toward them and provide them with fruits so they may be grateful.

points.label: Gratitude in Old Age
points.detail: Ibrahim (AS) affirmed that nothing in the heavens or earth is hidden from Allah, and praised Him for blessing him in his old age with Ismail and Ishaq - affirming that his Lord truly hears all prayers.

points.label: Prayer for Steadfastness and Forgiveness
points.detail: He concluded with a timeless supplication: "My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day the account is established.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Peace for Makkah and Protection From Idols: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) prayed: "My Lord, make this city (Makkah) peaceful and secure, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols." Recognizing that idols had misled many people, he affirmed that whoever follows his pure faith belongs to him, while leaving those who disobey to Allah's forgiveness and mercy.
• Settling His Family in a Barren Valley: Having left his wife Hajar and baby son Ismail in the empty desert of Makkah by Allah's command, Ibrahim (AS) prayed: "Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House so that they may establish prayer. So make people's hearts incline toward them and provide them with fruits so they may be grateful."
• Gratitude in Old Age: Ibrahim (AS) affirmed that nothing in the heavens or earth is hidden from Allah, and praised Him for blessing him in his old age with Ismail and Ishaq - affirming that his Lord truly hears all prayers.
• Prayer for Steadfastness and Forgiveness: He concluded with a timeless supplication: "My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day the account is established.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: This passage gives the Surah its name. Its full background is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (3364), where Ibn Abbas (RA) recounts Hajar's legendary faith when left in the barren valley: once she learned Allah had commanded it, she calmly said, "Then He will not let us perish". Also, in Sahih Muslim (202), Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) recited Ibrahim's words from verse 36 and wept out of compassion for his Ummah. Scholars note a profound lesson here: even Prophet Ibrahim (AS), who smashed idols with his own hands, still begged Allah to protect him and his children from idolatry - teaching believers never to feel overly secure about their own faith.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Never Think Allah Is Unaware of Oppressors

points.label: Delayed, Not Forgotten
points.detail: Allah reassures the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم): "Never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do!" He is only delaying them until a Day when their eyes will stare in horror, rushing forward with heads raised, unable to blink, and their hearts completely empty of hope.

points.label: Begging for a Second Chance
points.detail: Warn people of the Day punishment arrives, when the wrongdoers will plead: "Our Lord, delay us for a short time! We will answer Your call and follow the messengers." They will be reminded that they used to swear they would never decline - even though they lived in the very ruins of past wrongdoers and saw clearly how Allah dealt with them.

points.label: Allah's Plan Overrides All Plots
points.detail: The disbelievers plotted massive schemes, yet Allah knows every plot - even if their schemes were strong enough to move mountains. Never think Allah will break His promise to His messengers; Allah is Almighty and Lord of Retribution.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Delayed, Not Forgotten: Allah reassures the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم): "Never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do!" He is only delaying them until a Day when their eyes will stare in horror, rushing forward with heads raised, unable to blink, and their hearts completely empty of hope.
• Begging for a Second Chance: Warn people of the Day punishment arrives, when the wrongdoers will plead: "Our Lord, delay us for a short time! We will answer Your call and follow the messengers." They will be reminded that they used to swear they would never decline - even though they lived in the very ruins of past wrongdoers and saw clearly how Allah dealt with them.
• Allah's Plan Overrides All Plots: The disbelievers plotted massive schemes, yet Allah knows every plot - even if their schemes were strong enough to move mountains. Never think Allah will break His promise to His messengers; Allah is Almighty and Lord of Retribution.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir emphasizes that verse 42 is a pillar of comfort for oppressed believers in every era. When tyrants seem to escape accountability in this world, it is never because Allah is unaware - it is only a temporary respite before a Day when no plea for extra time will be accepted.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Day the Earth Changes and the Final Notification

points.label: A New Earth and Sky
points.detail: On that Day, this earth will be replaced with another earth, and the heavens as well, and every single soul will stand exposed before Allah, the One, the Prevailing (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar).

points.label: The Scene of the Criminals
points.detail: On that Day, you will see the criminals bound together in chains, wearing garments of liquid pitch (tar), with fire covering their faces.

points.label: Swift and Perfect Justice
points.detail: Allah will repay every single soul in full for what it earned - truly, Allah is swift in reckoning.

points.label: A Clear Message for All Humanity
points.detail: The Surah concludes by declaring: "This [Quran] is a clear notification (Balagh) for all humanity - so that they may be warned by it, know that He is only One God, and so that people of understanding may take heed.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• A New Earth and Sky: On that Day, this earth will be replaced with another earth, and the heavens as well, and every single soul will stand exposed before Allah, the One, the Prevailing (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar).
• The Scene of the Criminals: On that Day, you will see the criminals bound together in chains, wearing garments of liquid pitch (tar), with fire covering their faces.
• Swift and Perfect Justice: Allah will repay every single soul in full for what it earned - truly, Allah is swift in reckoning.
• A Clear Message for All Humanity: The Surah concludes by declaring: "This [Quran] is a clear notification (Balagh) for all humanity - so that they may be warned by it, know that He is only One God, and so that people of understanding may take heed.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: In Sahih al-Bukhari (6521) and Sahih Muslim (2790), the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) described the new earth of verse 48 as a pure, flat plain with no landmarks or mountains where all of humanity will be gathered. Ending the Surah by calling the Quran a Balagh (a clear, complete notification) ties the entire chapter together - from leading people out of darkness into light in verse 1, to delivering the final, unmistakable call to pure monotheism in verse 52.

stories_in_surah.snippet: • Search for Truth & Confronting Azar: Ibrahim grew up in Babylon. His father Azar was a chief craftsman of idols. Ibrahim observed the stars, the moon, and the sun, pointing out to his people that because these celestia...

stories_in_surah.title: The Epic Stories and Parables of Surah Ibrāhīm
stories_in_surah.content: According to classical scholars of Tafsir (such as Ibn Kathir and Al-Tabari) and authentic Hadith collections, these are the detailed accounts of the major stories and parables found in this chapter:

stories_in_surah.title: Prophet Musa (AS) and the "Days of Allah" (Verses 5-8)
stories_in_surah.content:
Before telling the stories of earlier destroyed nations, Allah shares the mission of Prophet Musa (Moses) to show that every prophet carried the same message of bringing people from darkness into light.

The Tafsir Details: Allah commanded Prophet Musa (AS) to remind the Children of Israel of the "Days of Allah" (Ayyamillah). Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir explain that the "Days of Allah" refer to both the great blessings Allah gave them and the terrible punishments He sent upon past oppressors.

Musa (AS) stood before his people and reminded them of their darkest days in Egypt under Pharaoh. Pharaoh's army had enslaved them, tortured them, slaughtered their baby boys, and kept their women alive to humiliate them. Allah miraculously rescued them from that nightmare.

Right after reminding them of this rescue, Musa (AS) delivered Allah's famous, universal promise in verse 7: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe." Musa (AS) then added a humbling reality check: even if every single person on earth became ungrateful and disbelieved, it would not harm Allah in the slightest - Allah is completely Free of Need and Worthy of all praise.

stories_in_surah.title: The Defiance of Past Nations: Nuh, 'Ad, and Thamud (Verses 9-17)
stories_in_surah.content:
To comfort Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) against the mockery of Makkah, Allah recounts the conversations between earlier messengers and their stubborn nations - specifically the people of Prophet Nuh (Noah), the mighty tribe of 'Ad, and the rock-carving tribe of Thamud.

The Tafsir Details: When these messengers came with clear miracles, their people literally pushed their hands into their mouths out of anger and mockery, saying they completely doubted the message. The messengers replied with simple, undeniable logic: "Can there be doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and earth?"

The arrogant leaders dismissed the prophets by saying, "You are only human beings like us!" The prophets humbly agreed - yes, they were human, but Allah chooses whomever He wills from His servants to receive revelation, and they could only trust in Allah.

Eventually, the disbelievers threatened the prophets: "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion." At that exact moment of extreme threat, Allah revealed His promise to the messengers: He would destroy the wrongdoers and let the believers inherit the land after them. Every stubborn, arrogant tyrant was brought to complete ruin, facing a terrifying punishment in Hell where they will be forced to sip boiling, foul water, surrounded by death from every side yet unable to die.

stories_in_surah.title: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in the Barren Valley of Makkah (Verses 35-41)
stories_in_surah.content:
This is the emotional heart of the Surah, recording the unforgettable moment when Prophet Ibrahim (AS) left his wife Hajar and his infant son Ismail in the empty, lifeless desert of Makkah by Allah's command.

The Tafsir Details: The full background of this moment is preserved in an authentic, detailed Hadith narrated by Ibn Abbas (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari (3364). Prophet Ibrahim (AS) traveled with Hajar and baby Ismail to the barren, rocky valley where the Kaaba would later stand - there was no water, no trees, and no people. He left them near a large tree with only a leather bag of dates and a small skin of water, and then turned to walk away.

Hajar followed him, calling out, "O Ibrahim! Where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no person and nothing at all?" He did not turn back. Finally, she asked, "Has Allah commanded you to do this?" He replied, "Yes." With extraordinary faith, Hajar said, "Then He will not let us perish."

Once Ibrahim (AS) walked out of their sight behind a mountain pass, he turned toward the sacred spot, raised his hands, and made the deeply moving supplications recorded in verses 35-41:

• For Peace and Pure Faith: "My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols."
• For His Family in the Desert: "Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful."
• For Prayer and Forgiveness: "My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established."

Allah answered every single word of his prayer: the miraculous spring of Zamzam gushed forth for Hajar and Ismail, the tribe of Jurhum settled there, Makkah became a thriving city of peace, and fruits from all over the world flow into that barren valley to this very day.

deep_dives.title: The Spiritual Power of the Surah (The Firm Word)
deep_dives.content:
Surah Ibrāhīm contains one of the most reassuring promises in the entire Quran for a believer facing death and the grave. In verse 27, Allah promises: "Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter."

In an authentic Hadith narrated by Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (RA) and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (4699) and Sahih Muslim (2871a), the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) explained that this verse was specifically revealed about the questioning in the grave. When a believer is laid to rest and questioned by the angels about their Lord, their religion, and their Prophet, Allah makes their heart and tongue firm so they answer with complete clarity: "There is no true god except Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

deep_dives.title: The Sermon of Shaytan on the Day of Judgment (Verse 22)
deep_dives.content:
This is one of the most chilling scenes in the entire Quran. After the final judgment is settled and the people of Paradise enter Paradise while the people of Hell enter Hell, Iblis (Shaytan) stands up in Hellfire and delivers a brutal, honest speech to his followers.

The Tafsir Details: According to Tafsir Ibn Kathir, when the people of Hell begin blaming Shaytan for misleading them, Shaytan cuts them off and tells them the cold truth:

• "Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you."
• "I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me."
• "So do not blame me; instead, blame yourselves! I cannot help you, and you cannot help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before."

For the very first time in history, the father of all lies speaks the complete truth - only after it is far too late for anyone to repent. It is a stark reminder that Shaytan can only whisper and invite; he can never force a human being to sin.

deep_dives.title: The Parable of the Two Trees: The Date Palm vs. The Bitter Vine (Verses 24-27)
deep_dives.content:
In these verses, Allah gives a vivid visual comparison between the word of true faith (La ilaha illallah) and the word of disbelief.

The Tafsir Details: Allah compares a "good word" to a "good tree": its roots are firmly planted deep in the ground, its branches reach high into the sky, and it gives its fruit in every season by its Lord's permission.

In an authentic Hadith recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (61, 4698) and Sahih Muslim (2811e), Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) once asked his companions a riddle: "Among the trees, there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like a Muslim. Tell me, what tree is it?" The companions started guessing different desert trees, while young Ibn Umar quietly thought to himself that it was the date palm, though he was too shy to speak in front of the elders. Finally, the Prophet (pbuh) smiled and revealed: "It is the date palm tree." Just like the date palm, every part of a true believer's faith is beneficial, steady, and constantly bearing good fruit.

In contrast, Allah compares an "evil word" (disbelief and falsehood) to an evil, bitter tree (identified by classical scholars as the colocynth or bitter gourd vine) that is easily uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no deep roots and no stability at all.

deep_dives.title: The Grand Finale: The Day the Earth Changes (Verses 42-52)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah closes with a powerful, unforgettable warning to oppressors and a final comfort to the believers.

The Tafsir Details: Allah tells the Prophet (pbuh) never to think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do - He is only delaying them until a Day when their eyes will stare in horror, their heads raised up, unable to blink, and their hearts completely empty of hope.

On that Day, this entire earth will be replaced with another earth, and the heavens as well, and every single soul will stand exposed before Allah, the One, the Prevailing. The Surah ends by declaring that this Quran is a clear notification (Balagh) for all of humanity - so that they may be warned by it, know with certainty that Allah is One God, and so that people of understanding may take heed.

Surah Ibrāhīm carries the believer from the darkest oppression of Pharaoh and the chilling honesty of Shaytan's sermon to the miraculous hope of Prophet Ibrahim's prayers in a barren desert, proving that a heart rooted in gratitude and pure faith will always stand firm in this life and the next.
